Maintenance Report — MNT-0010-007

Asset: WELL-0010 (SW-23 Well 010, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 29 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 30 Dec 2023 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 23 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0010-0060 on 2023-12-28 Report written: 01 Jan 2024

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0010-0060 at 13:15 on 2023-12-28 found crude oil on the pad: about 2.7% of the pad area, estimated 0.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.2 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 3% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 226 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 181 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 0.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0010-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.63% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0010-011

Asset: WELL-0010 (SW-23 Well 010, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 24 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 28 Aug 2024 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 104 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0010-0094 on 2024-08-22 Report written: 30 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0010-0094 showed the wellhead at 40.0 °C with the air at 35.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0010-024

Asset: WELL-0010 (SW-23 Well 010, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: separator Work started: 20 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 24 Feb 2026 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 103 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0010-0172 on 2026-02-19 Report written: 24 Feb 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator high-level alarm stayed on. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0010-0172 showed the wellhead at 17.3 °C with the air at 13.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.
